chief_complaint: Fever, arthralgias, and retro-orbital pain for 6 days.
history_of_present_illness: For 6 days, the patient experienced fever up to 40°C, arthralgias, and retro-orbital pain.
exposure_and_epidemiology: Patient returned from a 10-week trip to Thailand (Little Koh Chang, Hua Hin, Bangkok) the day before presentation and had not taken antimalarial chemoprophylaxis.
vitals: GCS 15/15, Temperature 39.1°C (102.4°F), BP 156/80 mmHg, pulse 106 bpm, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, SpO2 95% on ambient air.
physical_exam: No skin rash, no lymphadenopathy, clear chest auscultation, and no abdominal tenderness or organomegaly.
labs_and_diagnostics: FBC showed thrombocytopenia (81 x 10^9/L), elevated CRP (55 mg/L), AST (62 U/L), and ALT (106 U/L; dengue NS1 antigen test and rapid malaria diagnostic test were negative.
differential_diagnosis: Dengue fever, Chikungunya, Zika, Influenza, acute HIV infection, enteric fever, and malaria.
management_and_clinical_course: Serology for arboviruses, nasopharyngeal swab for influenza, fourth-generation HIV tests, blood cultures for enteric fever, and microscopy (thick and thin films) for malaria were initiated. Initial thick blood film showed Plasmodium species trophozoites (920/uL), but species were unclear, leading to admission and treatment with atovaquone/proguanil for 3 days, resulting in rapid recovery and discharge. Repeated microscopy and species-specific PCR confirmed mono-infection with P. knowlesi.
